newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen rejects higher Service bid.
newsitem.headline: Loewen rejects higher Service bid.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc. said Thursday its board unanimously rejected Service Corp International's sweetened $2.9 billion takeover bid and urged stockholders not to tender their shares to the offer.

Service, North America's biggest operator of funeral homes and cemeteries, last week offered US$45 a share in stock for Loewen, its closest competitor. Loewen previously rejected a US$43 a share offer.
In addition, Loewen said it filed an anti-trust lawsuit against Houston-based Service.

Loewen said its board concluded that "the best way to maximize value for shareholders is through continued implementation of the company's long-term business plan as an independent company. The Board believes the company will continue to build shareholder value through growth, especially growth through acquisitions, and through enhanced profitability."
Loewen's investment bankers, Smith Barney and Nesbitt Burns, gave the company opinions that the offer was inadequate, Loewen said.

Loewen said Service's offer was subject to "significant" conditions including the tendering of 75 percent of Loewen's outstanding common and preferred shares; SCI shareholder approval of the corporate reorganization of SCI and the issuance of shares in connection with the proposal; and the elimination of Loewen's shareholder rights plan.

Loewen said the "anti-competitive effects" of the deal have raised regulatory scrutiny in several states, including New York, Florida, Hawaii, Texas, California and Tennessee and from the Federal Trade Commission. It said the Canadian Competition Bureau is also investigating the deal.
This represents a broadening of regulatory scrutiny into the deal. Loewen previously said that Florida and the Federal Trade Commission were looking into the offer.
Loewen said its board adopted a severance plan for key executives that would be triggered by a change in control.
Loewen reiterated its claims that Service was seeking to buy it "on the cheap" and eliminate competition.
Its anti-trust case was filed against Service and its 40 percent owned affiliate Equity Corp International in U.S. District Court for the eastern district of New York.

The lawsuit alleges the deal would "substantially lessen competition in the markets for locally offered funeral and cemetery services, 'pre-need' funeral services, and the funeral home and cemetery acquisition markets."
It claims Service and Equity are conspiring to eliminate Loewen as a competitor.
